howToPlayPage.title: How to Play
howToPlayPage.heading: Dixo — Rules & Guide
howToPlayPage.description: A dice bluffing game for 2 to 6 players. Roll in secret, bid on what you think is out there, and call out the liars — or get caught bluffing yourself.

objective.title: Objective
objective.description: Be the last player with dice. Each round, players bid and bluff. Lose a challenge, lose a die. Run out of dice, you're out.

steps.title: A Round, Step by Step
steps.step1: At the start of each round, every player rolls their dice inside their cup and peeks at the result. Only you can see your own dice. Other players see only how many dice you have left.
steps.step2: The starting player announces a bid: a quantity and a face value. For example: 3 fours means you claim there are at least 3 dice showing a 4 across all players' dice combined.
steps.step3Intro: Going clockwise, each player must either:
steps.step3Raise: Raise the bid — increase the quantity, increase the face value (for the same quantity), or both.
steps.step3Challenge: Call "Challenge!" — if you think the previous bid is impossible.
steps.step4Intro: When a challenge is called, all cups are lifted and every die is counted:
steps.step4Correct: ≥ the bid quantity: the bid was correct → the challenger loses a die.
steps.step4Wrong: < the bid quantity: the bid was wrong → the bidder loses a die.
steps.step5: A new round begins. Players with 0 dice are eliminated. Play continues until one player remains.

paco.title: The Paco — Wild Dice
paco.description: In Dixo, dice showing a 1 (Paco) are wild. They count as any face value when resolving a bid on normal faces (2–6).
paco.example: Example: The bid is "4 fives". There are 3 fives and 2 Pacos in play → actual count = 5 → bid is correct.
paco.biddingOnPacos: Bidding on Pacos: When you bid on face 1 directly (e.g. "2 Pacos"), Pacos are no longer wild — only actual 1s count. To switch from a normal bid to a Paco bid, the quantity must be at least half (rounded up) of the previous bid quantity.
paco.switchingBack: Switching back to normal faces: Going from a Paco bid back to a normal face bid requires the quantity to be at least double the Paco quantity + 1. Example: "2 Pacos" → minimum normal bid is "5 [any face]".

elo.title: ELO Ranking
elo.description: Dixo uses a separate ELO for 1v1 and 4-player ranked games. Both start at 1,000. ELO is calculated based on the expected win probability vs. your opponent. The further apart your ratings, the more you gain (or lose) for an upset. Ranking is visible on the public leaderboard.

tips.title: Strategy Tips
tips.tip1: Count from your own dice. If you hold 2 fives and there are 10 dice in play, statistically expect ~1.7 more fives from other players. Use this to calibrate your bids.
tips.tip2: Don't always challenge a big bid. Sometimes letting a risky bid pass forces your opponent to keep raising until they overreach. Pick your challenges carefully.
tips.tip3: Bid on Pacos to reset the pressure. Switching to a Paco bid cuts the required quantity in half — useful when you're forced to make a bid you can't honestly raise.
tips.tip4: Watch the dice counts. A player down to 1 die is predictable — they can only have one value. Use that information to your advantage.
tips.tip5: In 4-player games, let others fight first. Conserving your dice while opponents knock each other out is a valid strategy — the last rounds are 1v1 and your dice count matters.
